overview.text: A bank official testified in court about N500 million in disbursements made from a Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) account to a private company during Sambo Dasuki's tenure as National Security Adviser.
The Guardian reports: NRS flags trillions in potential illicit financial flows
The Senate has approved President Bola Tinubu's request to refund ₦100.5 billion related to Yobe Airport.

cards.headline: Bank official testifies on N500m disbursements from ONSA account to private company during Dasuki’s tenure
cards.what_happened: A bank official testified in court about N500 million in disbursements made from a Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) account to a private company during Sambo Dasuki's tenure as National Security Adviser. The testimony concerns transfers of public funds to a private entity.
analysis: Why it matters: The testimony concerns transfers of public security funds from a government account to a private company, bearing on how public money was disbursed and to whom.
named: Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA)

cards.headline: NRS flags trillions in potential illicit financial flows
cards.what_happened: The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has flagged potential illicit financial flows totalling trillions of naira.

cards.headline: Yobe Airport: Senate approves Tinubu’s request to refund ₦100.5 billion
cards.what_happened: The Senate has approved President Bola Tinubu's request to refund ₦100.5 billion related to Yobe Airport. The development concerns public funds tied to a federal aviation asset.
analysis: Why it matters: The approval of a ₦100.5 billion refund involving public funds tied to a federal airport is a matter of public money oversight. The article does not state the refund's beneficiary or underlying basis, so the full implications cannot be assessed from it.

cards.headline: TotalEnergies begins Nigerias first deepwater exploration drilling
cards.what_happened: TotalEnergies has begun deepwater exploration drilling in Nigeria, according to the headline. The article body is restricted to paid subscribers, so no further details are available.
analysis: Why it matters: Deepwater exploration signals new upstream activity by a major operator in Nigeria, though the available text does not disclose ownership, contract or financial details.

cards.headline: NNPC achieves 100% pipeline availability after 20 years
cards.what_happened: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) has reported achieving 100% pipeline availability for the first time in 20 years, according to a Punch Newspapers headline. The article text provided contains no further detail on the figures, methods, or timeline behind the claim.
analysis: Why it matters: Pipeline availability affects the flow of crude and refined products that underpins public revenue and fuel supply, so official performance claims in this sector are relevant to public accountability. The provided text is only a headline, so the claim cannot be independently verified from it.
